classification.difficultyReason: Match each vehicle category to its stated percentage and calculate that percentage of the same supplied total.

content.prompt: In a city, $33\%$ of vehicles are utes, $18\%$ are four-wheel drives, $27\%$ are sedans and $22\%$ are station wagons. If there are $29\,700$ vehicles in the city, how many of each type of vehicle are there?

answer.short: Utes: $9801$; four-wheel drives: $5346$; sedans: $8019$; station wagons: $6534$.
answer.worked:
Utes:
$$\begin{align*}33\%\text{ of }29\,700&=\frac{33}{100}\times29\,700\\33\%\text{ of }29\,700&=9801\end{align*}$$
Four-wheel drives:
$$\begin{align*}18\%\text{ of }29\,700&=\frac{18}{100}\times29\,700\\18\%\text{ of }29\,700&=5346\end{align*}$$
Sedans:
$$\begin{align*}27\%\text{ of }29\,700&=\frac{27}{100}\times29\,700\\27\%\text{ of }29\,700&=8019\end{align*}$$
Station wagons:
$$\begin{align*}22\%\text{ of }29\,700&=\frac{22}{100}\times29\,700\\22\%\text{ of }29\,700&=6534\end{align*}$$
